mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-41.6 to -33.1 to -35.7 to -26.6), indicating an ongoing reopening trend; this momentum continues as consumers resume discretionary shopping and dining, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28 days despite the recent three-week uptrend persisting at decision time.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility improved from -33.4 to -25.4 over the snapshot, signaling gradual return of commuters; since commuters generate incidental retail trips (lunch, errands), continued WORKPLACES recovery drives RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks even though WORKPLACES continues its upward trajectory from t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has been declining (14.9 to 9.4), reflecting reduced home-confinement behavior; if RESIDENTIAL drops below 8.0, it signals a behavioral shift toward normal outside activity that will lift RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 14.9 to 9.4 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a drop of RESIDENTIAL below 8.0.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility (-51.0 to -43.6) and WORKPLACES (-33.4 to -25.4) are jointly recovering; their combined improvement indicates restored mobility infrastructure usage that interacts to amplify retail footfall more than either alone, driving RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together than when only one rises alone.

mechanism_narrative: If Victorian authorities reintroduce density or capacity restrictions on retail venues (a policy regime shift), RETAIL_REC will reverse its current recovery trend and decline over the next four weeks despite recent gains.
candidate_trigger: Announcement of renewed retail capacity restrictions or stage increase in restriction level
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC and WORKPLACES remain well below baseline, indicating restrictions are still only partially lifted
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 4 weeks even after a documented tightening of retail restrictions.

mechanism_narrative: The PARKS series is volatile (15.9, 43.0, 17.3, 20.9), suggesting outdoor recreation substitutes for indoor retail visits on nice-weather weeks; if PARKS spikes above 35 in a week, RETAIL_REC growth will be suppressed the following week as people substitute outdoor leisure for shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 35 points in a week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS peaked at 43.0 in t-2w while RETAIL_REC growth slowed the following week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a PARKS spike above 35, contradicting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-June falls in Melbourne's winter season, when colder weather historically reduces discretionary outdoor retail visits regardless of policy; this seasonal drag will cap further RETAIL_REC recovery and keep the next four weeks' mean flat or lower relative to the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2020-06-15 falls in Southern Hemisphere winter
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next four weeks despite the onset of winter, disconfirming the seasonal drag mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has not recovered as strongly as RETAIL_REC (TRANSIT still near -43.6 vs RETAIL_REC -26.6), implying increased reliance on private vehicles or local walking trips rather than public transit for shopping; if this gap between RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT recovery widens beyond 15 points, it signals a durable local-mobility pattern that will sustain RETAIL_REC gains over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: Gap between RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT recovery exceeds 15 points
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC at -26.6 vs TRANSIT at -43.6 in t-0w, a gap of 17 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth stalls or reverses over the next two weeks despite the RETAIL_REC-TRANSIT gap remaining above 15 points.
